utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't understand correctly. These additional two documents, are they going to be admitted as potential Defence exhibits, including these two transcripts? I didn't understand you, believe me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, they will be admitted as Defence exhibits if they have not already been entered as Prosecution exhibits. And although the court deputy has already indicated that his records do not show that they have already been admitted, I'm asking him to double-check that. But they will be admitted one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would also like to ask you something about document DD00-0286, although which I made a mistake. It concerns the testimony of General Nicolai. That's a letter under this number, and I would appreciate if this could marked for identification and admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You'll have to remind me a little more about that, that letter. General Nicolai testified last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I presented a letter at which point I didn't have an English translation. Later on it was found by the Prosecution. That's the letter which refers to the conversation between, as he claims, General Smith and Mladic. That's the letter I'm referring to. And the document, in my view, says that it was Nicolai who talked to Mladic through an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I, too, need to be reminded what this document was. My concern is that it was the note concerning a conversation between Ratko Mladic and an unknown person at General Smith's headquarters, and if that is the document that we're talking about, I believe that I had objected on the grounds of lack of foundation because General Nicolai said he did not participate in this conversation. But, as I say, I don't have my materials for General Nicolai at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the legal officer to investigate this matter and to report to me, and I'll give you the Chamber's decision on that when that report has been made to me. So I'm going to carry out my own investigation. Ms. Dedovic, that concludes your testimony. Thank you for giving it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, the Prosecution called Witness W-69, Afeza Karacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good day, Madam Witness.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court your full name.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: My name is Afeza Karacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you have any nicknames?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Hafiza.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: 3rd of May, 1963.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: In the municipality of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: For 26 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to the ICTY investigators on the 15th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What language did you give that statement in?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: In Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you re-read that statement before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you give another statement to ICTY investigators on the 20th of May, 2006?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What language did you give that statement in?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: In Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you gave the second statement, did you clarify a few things from your former statement?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is there anything today that you would want to clarify or correct from your more recent statement?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you re-read that second statement before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you say that these two statements are true and accurate representations of what you told the ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If asked the same questions today, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, pursuant to Rule 92 ter, I offer these two statements into evidence, one of 15 November 1995 and one of 20 May 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, they are admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P114 and P115, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: For the information of the Court, the questioning will be now in relation to sniping incident number 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, were you shot during the siege of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what date the incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: 23rd of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where were you when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: I was in a tram.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In which part of the tram were you standing?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: In the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In which direction was the tram going?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: From downtown towards my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what your neighbourhood is called?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Otoka.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Which direction in the tram were you facing?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: I was facing the back part of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you seated or were you standing?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In the summer of 2006 you met with an investigator of the ICTY and you indicated on camera the location of the incident on the 23rd of November, 1994. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to request the case manager, please, to show that video.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: "Investigator: I would like to ask you to come stand beside me and point to the location where the tram was at the time you were wounded. "Thank you. Can you please point in the direction the tram was moving at the time you were wounded. "Thank you. Could you please stand in the position you were standing at the time when you were wounded. "And could you please indicate where on your body you were wounded. "Thank you. And could you please point in the direction from which you believe the shot came that wounded you. "Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, would you say that this video is a true and accurate representation of what you told the investigators had occurred on the 23rd of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you give this information to the investigator entirely of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you say that the video we've just seen looks any different than that location did when the incident took place in 1994?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you indicate for the Court, please, where on your body the bullet entered.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the record please indicate that the witness is pointing to her upper right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And could you please indicate for the Court where the bullet exited your body.

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the record please indicate that the witness has pointed to a little bit further down on her right arm.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, when you pointed to the location from which you believe the shots came, what part of town is that, please?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Grbavica and the Jewish are on this side.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just for clarification, when you say "the Jewish," can you tell the Court what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know who was in control of these locations that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: I know. They were under the Serbian control.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What were you wearing on the day of the incident?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: A brown jacket and trousers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers on the tram on the day you were shot?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers near the incident on that day?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: No, apart from the IFOR or UNPROFOR, as it was at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you see any ABiH vehicles near the tram on that day?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall what the weather was like?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a clear day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was the tram crowded?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were there leaves on the trees on the day the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, from your own personal recollection, how many persons were injured in this same incident that you were injured in?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: One person was killed and there were another six wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you say "six," do you include yourself in the number six?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was the area where you were shot a dangerous area?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why did you decide to take the tram that day, knowing that it was a dangerous area?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: The whole city was an unsafe area; the place where I lived was unsafe, so it made no difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I would like to request the court officer to pull up a photograph, the 65 ter number is 2826, please. If I could request for assistance, I'd like to ask the witness to mark the photograph when it comes up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I know you have a little bit of difficulty marking things with that hand. Do you think you would be able to assist us in marking the location on this photograph where the tram was, approximately, on the day that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: Here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it possible for you to indicate for the Court the direction from which you believe the shots came? Is it possible for you to mark that in any way?

utterances.speaker: AFEZA KARACIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. No. I'm not entirely capable. This arrow ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: May I request the marked photograph, please, to be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Has she also indicated the direction from which the shots came?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That was the last question, Your Honour, but she says she tried to draw an arrow but had a little bit of difficulty. She's not as adept after the incident in using her hand to draw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It may be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just one question for you, Witness, please. You say that you were hit by a sniper who must have been somewhere in Grbavica or in the Jewish cemetery, in that area. So why are you so sure? What makes you so sure? Is it a conclusion that you draw yourself out of very objective statements or conclusions, or is it because you were told that that is probably where the shooter was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I came at this conclusion because these first high-rise buildings behind the museum is the place where the sniper was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that's my question. How can you know that the sniper was in that high-rise? That high-rise actually is ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because he couldn't have been at the first two ones closer to the tram tracks. He must have been further beyond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the case manager, please, to show us the 360-degree ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are at the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we'll break now and resume tomorrow. Is it in the morning or afternoon? Afternoon. Tomorrow afternoon at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
